timing.note: DOH's own Section 8 list is closed (page dated Aug 20, 2026). Register at cthcvp.org/notifications.

steps.title: Know the state list is closed
steps.detail: The Department of Housing (DOH) Section 8 list is closed. DOH reopens it only after enough families on it have been served.

steps.title: Sign up for opening alerts
steps.detail: Register at cthcvp.org/notifications to hear when any Section 8 program in Connecticut opens its list.

steps.title: Watch for the opening notice
steps.detail: Before it opens, DOH and local newspapers publish a notice and pre-application form.

steps.title: Ask local housing authorities
steps.detail: Many run their own Section 8 programs. Ask when their list opens, whether they prefer local residents, and how long the wait is.

timing.note: Register at cthcvp.org to be told when it reopens.

steps.title: Know the RAP list is closed
steps.detail: The state Rental Assistance Program (RAP) list is closed, with no reopening date.

steps.title: Register at cthcvp.org
steps.detail: Sign up to be told when RAP opens its list.

steps.title: Watch for the notice and form
steps.detail: A notice and pre-application form will appear in local newspapers and on the DOH website.

steps.title: Apply through the local housing authority
steps.detail: Once open, the local housing authority checks your household, income and assets and puts eligible families on its waiting list.

steps.title: Wait to be contacted
steps.detail: When your family is chosen, the housing authority contacts you and issues a certificate.

timing.item: New Haven (Elm City Communities) Section 8 list

steps.title: Know the list is closed
steps.detail: Elm City Communities (New Haven's housing authority) closed its Section 8 list at 11:59pm on May 1, 2026.

steps.title: Already on it? Keep your info current
steps.detail: The closure doesn't affect people on the list. Report any change of address, email, phone or household; returned mail or a missed deadline cancels your application.

steps.title: Check your status online
steps.detail: Use the Applicant Portal at elmcitycommunities.org/waiting-list to get a registration code, check status and update your record.

steps.title: Watch for the reopening
steps.detail: It will be posted on the Elm City Communities website, in local newspapers and on 211.

steps.title: Ask for an accommodation if needed

timing.value: Opened Sept 10–17, 2026 (lottery for 3,000); current status not posted
timing.note: Check hartfordhousing.org for the next opening.

steps.title: Know which list is which
steps.detail: The Hartford Housing Authority's public housing list (apartments it owns) is separate from Section 8. Its Section 8 list is closed.

steps.title: Check the public housing list status
steps.detail: Use "Check Public Housing Waiting List" on hartfordhousing.org (hartfordhousing.myhousing.com). Main phone: 860.723.8400.

steps.title: Watch for the next opening
steps.detail: The last opening was Sept 10–17, 2026, with online pre-applications and a lottery that picked 3,000 for the list.

steps.title: For Section 8, check other agencies
steps.detail: The housing authority points to cthcvp.org for Connecticut agencies that open their lists.

timing.note: 567 with no services (48 emergency, 519 urgent), 310 underserved, 675 future needs. The count is for DDS residential supports, mostly people with intellectual disability; autistic adults without intellectual disability are served through the DSS autism waiver.

steps.title: Become DDS-eligible
steps.detail: First the person must be found eligible for the Department of Developmental Services (DDS). Help: 1-866-433-8192 or 1-860-418-6117.

steps.title: Get a case manager or Help Line
steps.detail: If on Medicaid, you get a case manager; if not, the DDS Help Line assists you.

steps.title: Raise the housing need at planning
steps.detail: At the yearly planning meeting, the case manager's assessments sort an unmet housing need as emergency, urgent or future.

steps.title: Get your priority status
steps.detail: A regional team tells you your status: the Waiting List (emergency, or need within a year) or the Planning List (need in 2+ years).

steps.title: When funding comes, enroll in a waiver
steps.detail: You and the case manager build a plan and budget, and you apply for Medicaid and a DDS home and community waiver. DDS says services aren't guaranteed.

timing.note: From CT Public reporting; DSS confirms a waiting list applies. DSS says impairments must be diagnosed before 22; the DDS application asks for an autism test before 21.

steps.title: Check the basic eligibility
steps.detail: The Department of Social Services (DSS) autism waiver needs a main diagnosis of autism, an IQ of 70 or higher, and major limits in at least two areas such as self-care, language, learning or living on your own.

steps.title: Fill out the application
steps.detail: Print the application (English or Spanish). On page 2, mark that you're applying for the Autism Spectrum Disorder Program.

steps.title: Gather the checklist documents
steps.detail: Testing, medical history, a health-privacy (HIPAA) form, proof of Connecticut residence and ID copies. If something's missing, fill out the Release of Information form.

steps.title: Send it to the DDS Eligibility Unit
steps.detail: Mail: 460 Capitol Avenue, Hartford, CT 06106. Fax: 860-622-2797. Email: DDS.Eligibility@ct.gov.

steps.title: Expect a waiting list
steps.detail: The waiver isn't an entitlement and a waiting list applies. It doesn't provide housing placement or rent help.

timing.note: Psych and educational testing through age 17. Make sure testing is done by these ages.

steps.title: Get the application
steps.detail: Print the DDS application in English or Spanish, or email DDS.Eligibility@ct.gov to get one by mail.

steps.title: Mark the autism program
steps.detail: On page 2, show you're applying for the Autism Spectrum Disorder Program.

steps.title: Gather testing and records
steps.detail: Psychological and educational testing through age 17, and a standard autism test before age 21. Also medical history, a recent physical, a HIPAA form, guardianship papers if any, proof of residence, and copies of IDs and school records.

steps.title: Fill gaps with a release form
steps.detail: If anything's missing, complete the Release of Information form (page 7 of the application).

steps.title: Submit to the Eligibility Unit
steps.detail: 460 Capitol Avenue, Hartford, CT 06106; fax 860-622-2797; DDS.Eligibility@ct.gov. Help: 1-866-433-8192 or 1-860-418-6117.

steps.title: If denied, ask about a hearing
steps.detail: The DDS page links to how to request a hearing.

timing.value: End of school year (June 30) in which student turns 22
timing.note: Or earlier with a regular diploma. This is when adult DDS/DSS services usually take over.

steps.title: Know the end date
steps.detail: Special education lasts through the school year in which the student turns 22 (school years end June 30), or until graduation with a regular diploma, whichever comes first.
steps.time: Through June 30 of the year they turn 22

steps.title: Check the exit plan in the IEP
steps.detail: The IEP lists the planned exit: a regular diploma or reaching the maximum age. The school's planning team decides whether it's been met.

steps.title: If you disagree, use dispute options
steps.detail: Parents and adult students can challenge the decision using the options in the Procedural Safeguards Notice.

timing.note: SPA CT-26-0023 ended the 1915(i) CHESS benefit.

steps.title: Call CHRO's Housing Discrimination Unit
steps.detail: The Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities: (800) 477-5737 ext. 3403 (toll free in CT) or (860) 541-3403; TDD (860) 541-3459.

steps.title: Act early
steps.detail: A formal complaint must be filed within 300 days, and writing and filing it takes time.

steps.title: Keep a record of contacts
steps.detail: Note every meeting and call with the landlord, manager, agent or loan officer: name, title, place, date and time.

steps.title: Write it down and save papers
steps.detail: Write down what happened and keep receipts, applications and other documents.

steps.title: Know your other options
steps.detail: Report crimes such as threats to local police. You can also contact HUD at 1-800-669-9777 or a local fair housing agency.
